tags.name: Intel hybrid CPU (P-cores and E-cores)
tags.hint: 12th to 14th gen Core and Core Ultra. Thread Director and the Windows scheduler stay in charge of core placement.
tags.description: Set for Intel CPUs with performance and efficient cores. Items that park E-cores, pin affinities or override the heterogeneous scheduling policy are kept out of presets on this tag, and Power Throttling stays on.

tags.name: Intel Raptor Lake desktop CPU
tags.hint: 13th and 14th gen desktop Core. The microcode 0x12F (Vmin Shift) check runs, and idle-voltage-raising items are blocked.
tags.description: Set for 13th and 14th generation desktop processors affected by the Vmin Shift instability. The health report checks for microcode 0x12F or newer, and items that keep the cores at high voltage while idle, such as disabling processor idle, are blocked.

tags.name: AMD Ryzen (Zen)
tags.hint: AMD Ryzen desktop or laptop CPU. The AMD chipset driver is checked and the power plan follows the preset.
tags.description: Set for AMD Zen processors. The health report checks that the AMD chipset driver is installed, because it provides the power plan integration and scheduler hints Windows relies on.

tags.name: AMD Ryzen X3D (single CCD)
tags.hint: Single-CCD X3D CPU such as the 7800X3D or 9800X3D. Chipset driver check plus normal plan selection.
tags.description: Set for X3D processors with one core complex. All cores share the 3D V-Cache, so no core-steering is needed; the chipset driver check and the preset's power plan apply.

tags.name: AMD Ryzen X3D (dual CCD)
tags.hint: 7900X3D, 7950X3D, 9900X3D, 9950X3D. Keeps Balanced with core parking and Game Bar game detection for the V-Cache CCD.
tags.description: Set for X3D processors with two core complexes. Games are steered to the V-Cache CCD by the AMD 3D V-Cache optimizer driver, which needs the Balanced plan with core parking and Game Bar game detection. Ultimate or High performance plans, core-parking changes and Game Bar removal are blocked on this tag.

tags.name: NVIDIA GPU
tags.hint: An NVIDIA GeForce or RTX GPU is active. Guidance covers Reflex and driver settings; driver profiles are never written.
tags.description: Set when an NVIDIA GPU is active. iG Windows Tuner shows read-only guidance (Reflex, G-SYNC, Resizable BAR) and never writes NVIDIA driver profiles.

tags.name: AMD Radeon GPU
tags.hint: An AMD Radeon GPU is active. Guidance covers Anti-Lag and driver settings; driver profiles are never written.
tags.description: Set when an AMD Radeon GPU is active. iG Windows Tuner shows read-only guidance such as Anti-Lag and Smart Access Memory, and never writes driver profiles.

tags.name: Intel GPU
tags.hint: An Intel integrated or Arc GPU is active. Guidance only; driver settings are never written.
tags.description: Set when an Intel GPU is active, integrated or discrete. iG Windows Tuner shows read-only guidance and never writes driver settings.

tags.name: Intel Arc discrete GPU
tags.hint: Intel Arc graphics card. Resizable BAR is required for good performance, so its status is checked and shown.
tags.description: Set for Intel Arc discrete GPUs, which depend on Resizable BAR for usable performance. The health report treats a disabled Resizable BAR as a problem and explains the firmware setting.

tags.name: Desktop PC
tags.hint: No battery detected. Desktop power plans and AC-only tuning apply.
tags.description: Set when the PC has no system battery. Power items only need AC values, and laptop overlays do not apply.

tags.name: Laptop
tags.hint: A battery is present. AC and DC values are separate, and battery-saving behaviour on DC is never reduced.
tags.description: Set when a system battery is present. Power items keep separate AC and DC values, presets never reduce battery saving on DC, and the Ultimate plan is not used.

tags.name: Modern Standby (S0)
tags.hint: The PC uses Modern Standby. Windows power-mode overlays are preferred over custom power plans.
tags.description: Set when the firmware uses Modern Standby instead of S3 sleep. On these systems Microsoft recommends the power-mode overlays (Best performance and so on) over custom plans, so presets use those.

tags.name: Intel I225 Ethernet
tags.hint: Intel I225 2.5 GbE controller. Known-issue notes and the vendor's advanced-property keywords apply.
tags.description: Set for Intel I225 2.5 GbE controllers. The network page shows the known issues for this family (early steppings, Energy Efficient Ethernet) and maps the vendor's advanced-property keywords.

tags.name: Intel I226 Ethernet
tags.hint: Intel I226 2.5 GbE controller. Known-issue notes and the vendor's advanced-property keywords apply.
tags.description: Set for Intel I226 2.5 GbE controllers. The network page shows the known issues for this family and maps the vendor's advanced-property keywords.

tags.name: Realtek Ethernet
tags.hint: Realtek Ethernet controller. Vendor-specific advanced-property names and known issues apply.
tags.description: Set for Realtek Ethernet controllers. Realtek drivers use their own advanced-property names for power-saving features, which this tag maps to the standard keywords.

tags.name: Marvell / Aquantia Ethernet
tags.hint: Marvell (Aquantia) multi-gigabit Ethernet controller. Vendor keyword mapping and known issues apply.
tags.description: Set for Marvell AQtion (formerly Aquantia) controllers. The tag maps their advanced-property names and shows known issues for this family.

tags.name: Killer networking
tags.hint: Killer Ethernet or Wi-Fi with its traffic-prioritisation software. Conflicting QoS items are flagged.
tags.description: Set for Killer network adapters. Their prioritisation service can conflict with Windows policy-based QoS, so iG Windows Tuner points this out before applying game QoS.

tags.name: NVMe system disk
tags.hint: Windows runs from an NVMe SSD. Storage items keep TRIM and the default write caching.
tags.description: Set when the system drive is an NVMe SSD. Health checks confirm TRIM is enabled; no storage tuning beyond Windows defaults is applied.

tags.name: SATA SSD system disk
tags.hint: Windows runs from a SATA SSD. Storage items keep TRIM and the default write caching.
tags.description: Set when the system drive is a SATA solid-state drive. Health checks confirm TRIM is enabled.

tags.name: Hard disk system drive
tags.hint: Windows runs from a spinning hard disk. SysMain and memory compression stay on because they help here.
tags.description: Set when the system drive is a hard disk. SysMain (prefetching) and memory compression noticeably help on hard disks, so items that turn them off are blocked on this tag.

tags.name: Less than 16 GB of RAM
tags.hint: Under 16 GB of memory. SysMain and memory compression stay on, and memory-hungry items are blocked.
tags.description: Set when installed memory is below 16 GB. Memory compression and SysMain stay on, because turning them off increases paging on small-memory systems.

tags.name: 16 GB of RAM
tags.hint: 16 GB of installed memory. Standard memory behaviour applies.
tags.description: Set when installed memory is 16 GB (up to but not including 32 GB). No memory-specific overlay changes are made.

tags.name: 32 GB of RAM
tags.hint: 32 GB of installed memory. Standard memory behaviour applies.
tags.description: Set when installed memory is 32 GB (up to but not including 64 GB). No memory-specific overlay changes are made.

tags.name: 64 GB or more of RAM
tags.hint: 64 GB or more of installed memory. Standard memory behaviour applies.
tags.description: Set when installed memory is 64 GB or more. No memory-specific overlay changes are made by default.

tags.name: Virtual machine
tags.hint: Running inside a virtual machine. Hardware-level items (devices, firmware, power hardware) are disabled.
tags.description: Set when Windows runs in a virtual machine, including Windows Sandbox. Items that change physical devices, interrupts, firmware-backed features or power hardware do not apply and are disabled.
